name: readability
description: Write everything in plain English that a grade 7-9 reader can follow, based on readability-score practice (Flesch Reading Ease, Flesch-Kincaid, Gunning Fog, SMOG). Target Flesch Reading Ease 60-70: sentences under 20 words on average, any sentence over 25 words split into two or three, one idea per sentence, active voice in at least 90% of sentences, short common words over long formal ones, paragraphs of 2-3 sentences, and headings, lists and tables in long documents. The scope is ALL prose Claude writes, with no exceptions — chat replies, plans, summaries, commit messages, PR titles and bodies, issue and review comments, README and doc prose, log and error strings, artifact and UI text. Technical material stays byte-exact: code, identifiers, commands, paths, URLs, regexes, version numbers and quoted output are never reworded, only the prose around them. Accuracy never drops for simplicity. Always-on via hooks, with a self-audit before every delivery. Each turn a hook also measures the readability of Claude's previous reply — Flesch Reading Ease and grade, read from the session transcript with code and tables stripped out — and feeds the score back as a reference point, so the next reply is calibrated against a real number instead of a guess.
